title: Trigger a customer meeting prep request
description: Register a calendar Trigger through the Platform Triggers API and deliver one signed event to a small receiver that prints a customer-meeting prep request.

questions.prompt: What is your work email? It is used once to discover your Glean tenant.
What distinctive meeting-title substring should trigger prep, such as Customer QBR?
What public HTTPS URL ending in /webhook should receive the signed event?

prerequisites: The Platform Triggers API enabled for the tenant
A calendar trigger preset that advertises a time_offset, normally GCAL_1
A public HTTPS URL for the receiver, such as a temporary cloudflared tunnel
A bearer token that Glean may send to the receiver

demoQueries.query: Deliver one signed event for a customer meeting whose title matches the configured pattern.
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: The receiver verifies the bearer token and Standard Webhooks signature, prints a Customer meeting prep request with the title, start time, and event URL, and does not call any downstream system.

demoQueries.query: Delete the trigger after the test.
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: The recipe deletes only the trigger ID saved by its own setup command and clears the local signing secret.

codeAssets.description: Signed webhook receiver plus Platform Triggers preset discovery and trigger lifecycle

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.description: This recipe uses Node's built-in HTTP server and fetch; there is no external automation platform or downstream write dependency.

steps.title: Run the fixture verification
steps.description: Verify preset selection, experimental Platform API headers, input resolution, and Standard Webhooks signing before connecting a tenant.

steps.title: Sign in to Glean
steps.description: Use @gleanwork/auth for tenant discovery and refreshable OAuth credentials stored outside the project. If OAuth is unavailable, provide a user-scoped token with the Triggers permission as a CI fallback.

steps.title: Configure the meeting pattern and receiver
steps.description: Set GLEAN_TRIGGER_INPUT_TITLE to a distinctive title substring such as Customer QBR, choose the preset ID returned by the catalog, and set GLEAN_WEBHOOK_URL to a public HTTPS URL ending in /webhook. Set a bearer token that the receiver will accept.

steps.title: Start and expose the receiver
steps.description: The receiver listens on loopback, verifies bearer delivery auth and the Standard Webhooks signature, and prints a prep request for matching meeting titles. Expose /webhook through a public HTTPS tunnel before registering the trigger.

steps.title: Register the Platform Trigger
steps.description: Setup reads GET /api/trigger-presets and the selected preset detail, then creates one trigger through POST /api/triggers. It saves the returned trigger ID and signing secret locally.

steps.title: Test one signed delivery
steps.description: Send one fixture delivery through the same signed webhook contract without waiting for a calendar event. Then schedule one real matching meeting to verify forward delivery from the Platform Trigger.

steps.title: Delete the trigger
steps.description: Delete only the trigger ID created by this recipe and clear the local signing secret.

architecture.label: Glean Platform Trigger
architecture.caption: Preset discovery, registration, and signed delivery

architecture.label: Prep receiver
architecture.caption: Prints a focused request without writing downstream

aiPrompt: Scaffold the customer-meeting-prep-trigger recipe. Ask for a work email, a distinctive calendar meeting-title substring, and a public HTTPS webhook URL ending in /webhook. Use @gleanwork/auth for tenant discovery, Authorization Code with PKCE, and refreshable OAuth credentials stored outside the project; accept a user-provided token only as a CI fallback. Discover the live preset catalog with GET /api/trigger-presets, read the selected preset detail, and create the trigger with POST /api/triggers. Send x-glean-include-experimental: true on every Platform Triggers request. Configure a 1,800-second time_offset only when the selected preset advertises it. Run the included signed receiver and verify one fixture delivery before asking the reader to schedule a real matching meeting. Never use legacy /rest/api/v1 routes, Cursor, n8n, or a downstream write. Save and later delete only the trigger ID created by this recipe.
llmContext: The Platform Triggers API is experimental and requires x-glean-include-experimental: true. @gleanwork/auth supplies a refreshable triggers-scoped OAuth token and uses GLEAN_API_TOKEN as its standard user-scoped fallback when present. The list response identifies presets; GET /api/trigger-presets/{preset_id} carries the authoritative inputs. Create with POST /api/triggers using preset_id, inputs, and delivery.webhook_url plus bearer auth. The response returns trigger_id and signing_secret once. Delivery uses Standard Webhooks headers webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, and webhook-signature over the raw body; reject stale timestamps and invalid signatures. The receiver must re-check the meeting title because delivery is untrusted. Use TRIGGERS_READ/TRIGGERS_WRITE Platform permissions; the cookbook's TRIGGERS auth label is the current compatibility convention.

content.problem: A customer meeting is about to start, but the team still has to reconstruct the account context manually. The first useful step is simply knowing that a matching meeting event arrived and turning it into a focused prep request.
takeItFurther: Pass the meeting and account context to the Triage or Account Brief Agent after the delivery contract is reliable.
Add a read-only preview that gathers recent account changes before writing anything downstream.
Use the same receiver pattern with a different tenant-supported content-event preset.

guardrails.title: One trigger, one receiver
guardrails.rule: The quickstart creates one trigger and prints one prep request; it does not connect a tracker, Slack, Cursor, or n8n.

guardrails.title: Verify before acting
guardrails.rule: The receiver verifies bearer auth, timestamp freshness, and the Standard Webhooks signature before inspecting the event.

limitations.title: A public HTTPS endpoint is required
limitations.description: Glean cannot deliver to localhost directly. Use a temporary HTTPS tunnel for the beginner walkthrough and keep the URL private.

limitations.title: Preset availability is tenant-specific
limitations.description: The recipe refuses to guess a preset ID and only registers a preset returned by the connected tenant's catalog.
